abstract_summary: End-to-end deep learning pipelines for camera-radar 3D object detection are well established in driver assistance systems and autonomous vehicles; however, adapting them to roadside-mounted infrastructure presents significant challenges. evidence.excerpt:
end-to-end models prone to failure and difficult to
adapt without massive location-specific datasets. Hence, instead of
designing a complex end-to-end pipeline for direct 3D bounding
box estimation, a low-cost, resource-efficient two-stage approach
is proposed for real-time 3D shape and orientation estimation.
The first stage utilizes any off-the-shelf, state-of-the-art method
to extract 2D camera bounding boxes and associated 3D radar
points for each road user. The proposed second stage then
processes these inputs to construct 3D oriented bounding boxes
where radar data determines 3D position, predefined templates
define size for each road user, and a tiny neural network
predicts a site-specific and optimized yaw angle. The algorithm
is successfully validated at a curved road with a junction for
pedestrians, bicycles, and cars, where it achieves25frames per
second on an NVIDIA Jetson

Manually labeled 3D bounding boxes from the lidar sensor
serve as the ground truth (GT) data in this work. Distinct
datasets are dedicated to training and validating theYawPredic-
tionNetmodels. At the same time, a separate, independent set
of500frames containing451persons,360bicycles, and299
cars is reserved exclusively for validating the final 3D OBB
outcome of the proposed methodology and is omitted from
parameter tuning. To prevent temporal data leakage, dataset
splits are created using sequence-disjoint segments rather than
random frame sampling. This frame count was strategically
chosen as manual 3D annotation of dense point clouds is
exceptionally labor-intensive, yet the total count of over1100
well-distributed dynamic object instances across these frames

Training and validation forYawPredictionNetmodels for
bicycles and cars is performed using AdamW (initial learn-
ing rate10 −3, batch size1, gradient clip0.5) with a
ReduceLROnPlateauscheduler (patience 50 epochs) op-
timizingL total =L MSE(sinψ) +L MSE(cosψ). Class-specific

VI. CONCLUSION
This paper presented a low-cost, resource-efficient two-stage
framework for real-time 3D shape and orientation estimation
of pedestrians, bicycles, and cars using roadside camera-radar

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Final 3D bounding box errors are measured against dense LiDAR ground truth on a sequence-disjoint holdout set of 500 frames that was excluded from template tuning and YawPredictionNet training.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Direct 3D metric errors (centroid, dimensions, yaw) against manually labeled LiDAR ground truth on the independent validation set.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: MSE loss on sin/cos yaw against LiDAR-derived labels for YawPredictionNet, plus manual scaling-factor and template-bound tuning on a separate development split.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported claims of real-time edge execution, resource efficiency, and improved spatial positioning over vision baselines are well supported by the experimental data and ablation studies.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The system is quantitatively evaluated on a sequence-disjoint holdout set of 500 frames containing over 1,100 road user instances against 3D LiDAR ground truth, demonstrating substantial improvements over monocular homography baselines and achieving 25 FPS on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin edge platform.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluation is conducted on a sequence-disjoint holdout set of 500 frames against dense 3D LiDAR annotations not used during template tuning or yaw network training.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Direct 3D metric bounding box errors (centroid x/y/z, length, width, height, and yaw) measured against ground-truth 3D bounding boxes from dense LiDAR.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: MSE loss on trigonometric yaw representations (sinψ, cosψ) against training labels from LiDAR for YawPredictionNet, and manual parameter tuning on a separate development split for extent scaling factors.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly note that evaluation was conducted at a single roadside installation, fixed template bounds limit adaptability across vehicle sub-types, and yaw prediction models are site-optimized.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed: Stage 1 associates 2D camera detections (YOLOv11) with clustered 3D radar returns (DBSCAN), and Stage 2 computes 3D centroid and height via calibrated projections, bounds bounding box extents using class-specific geometric templates, and regresses yaw using a tiny multi-modal neural network (YawPredictionNet).
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a clear, well-scoped engineering contribution with sound technical formulations, complete calibration details, thorough ablation studies, and objective benchmarking on an independent holdout set against ground truth.
primary.scoped_contribution: A resource-efficient two-stage pipeline for roadside 3D bounding box estimation and orientation of road users using an RGB camera and 3D radar, coupling geometric templates with a compact yaw prediction network.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a clear, well-scoped engineering contribution with sound technical formulations, complete calibration details, thorough ablation studies, and objective benchmarking on an independent holdout set against ground truth.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly note that evaluation was conducted at a single roadside installation, fixed template bounds limit adaptability across vehicle sub-types, and yaw prediction models are site-optimized.
